## 固定收益開篇論點

7月31日紐約收盤，美國公債結束前一交易日的盤整，再度全面遭到拋售。2年期殖利率上升5個基點至4.28%，5年期與10年期各上升7個基點，分別收在4.45%與4.75%；30年期則上升6個基點至5.27%。7月30日各指標天期僅上升1個基點，週五賣壓則從政策敏感的短端一路延伸至長端。10年期殖利率也升破聯準會會議後高點，長債殖利率逼近2007年以來最高區間。

本波行情最主要的變化，是市場對聯準會延後緊縮做出更嚴厲的判斷。聯邦公開市場委員會以9比3決議，將聯邦基金利率區間維持在3.5%至3.75%；三位異議官員均警告，現在按兵不動，日後可能被迫更大幅緊縮。這番訊息直接反映在價格上：賣壓先從2年至5年期展開，隨後向較長天期擴散，投資人開始要求更高的持續性通膨補償。第2季就業成本上升0.9%，高於預估中位數；6月PCE物價雖下跌0.1%，就業成本數據仍未帶來市場所需的明確薪資通膨降溫訊號。

油價與海外利率又加重政策挑戰。週末前供給疑慮升溫，WTI上漲1.29%至$84.67，Brent上漲1.22%至$90.12。歐元區通膨加速至2.9%，其中能源價格上漲10%，帶動德國公債殖利率上揚，也強化市場對歐洲央行再次升息的預期。因此，美國公債遭到拋售，不能只歸因於主席Kevin Warsh的溝通溢價。真正的組合是政策反應函數更難預測，加上最新數據顯示，薪資與能源壓力可能讓各地通膨負擔延續。

不過，行情結構並不支持把整波走勢都視為通膨預期衝擊。10年期實質殖利率上升6個基點至2.47%，解釋名目殖利率7個基點漲幅的大部分；10年期損益兩平通膨率僅上升1個基點至2.28%。以7月全月來看，10年期實質殖利率上升27個基點，名目殖利率上升31個基點。市場要求更高的實質報酬，政策路徑仍不確定，再融資公告又即將公布；這些因素的重要性，遠高於通膨補償預期全面脫錨。

信用與跨資產市場有序，避免利率衝擊演變成全面平倉。LQD受存續期間曝險拖累，下跌0.15%；HYG與JNK則近乎持平。S&P 500上漲0.70%，VIX下跌6.44%至15.99；即使美國殖利率走高，美元仍下跌0.21%。然而，較弱環節的融資紀律確實收緊：Cable One為履行強制收購義務籌措約$10億，交易卻陷入困境；Extenet的資產擔保債券未能支付利息；大量供給則使市政債經歷異常疲弱的7月。市場流動性依然正常，但高實質殖利率正暴露融資結構、再融資依賴與個別發行人的內控缺失。

因此，本次收盤延續並加深聯準會會議後的市場狀態，並未開啟新一輪成長恐慌。近期政策寬鬆的可能性早已消退；週五進一步證明，即使長端仍含有財政與公信力溢價，短端也可能向上重新定價。日本央行釋出鷹派指引並強力干預日圓，降低日本輸入性通膨壓力，帶來部分制衡；但日本資產報酬提高，以及外匯存底操作可能產生外溢效應，又構成另一面風險。當前固定收益市場的核心問題，是即將公布的美國數據與穩定的美國公債附息券發行指引，能否在個別信用壓力擴大成更廣泛的承接問題前，先把實質殖利率壓低。

## 美國公債利率、Fed定價、實質殖利率與曲線結構

週五賣壓相當全面，僅略偏向曲線中段，並未再次出現大幅陡峭化。5年期與10年期殖利率各上升7個基點，2年期上升5個基點，30年期上升6個基點。2s10s利差擴大2個基點至47個基點，2s30s則陡峭化1個基點至99個基點。這與7月29日聯準會按兵不動後，2年期殖利率下滑、30年期大幅上升的反應不同。週五行情收回大部分短端利多，卻幾乎完整保留會後形成的長端溢價。

從全月來看，殖利率曲線發出的緊縮訊號，遠強於單日小幅陡峭化所呈現的程度。7月底2年期殖利率較月初上升14個基點，5年期上升26個基點，10年期上升31個基點，30年期上升36個基點。漲幅隨天期拉長而擴大，反映的遠不只是一次升息預期，還包括持續性通膨、未來龐大融資需求與政策指引有限等風險。即使下次FOMC決策延後，這些因素仍可能讓均衡折現率維持高檔。

三位異議官員清楚點出近期政策傳導路徑。克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack認為政策限制性仍不足；明尼亞波利斯聯準銀行總裁Neel Kashkari支持隨數據公布逐步緊縮；達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Lorie Logan則表示，現在採取溫和行動，可降低日後大幅緊縮的必要性。即使考量供給衝擊與生產力因素，Logan仍判斷通膨正朝2%區間中段移動，而不是回到2%。三人共同關切的，不只是7月能源價格波動，而是勞動需求、支出與金融情勢依然過強，通膨很難自行走完回歸目標的最後一段路。

就業成本在同一交易日檢驗了這項論點。第2季就業成本上升0.9%，高於預估中位數。超出預期的幅度尚不足以單獨證明薪資重新加速，但當市場正等待更低的通膨數據來驗證聯準會保持耐心是否合理時，意外的方向格外重要。再加上油價上漲，短端最初的賣壓因而蔓延至承擔較長期通膨與期限溢價風險的天期。2年期殖利率收在4.28%，仍低於聯邦基金利率區間中點4.37%，代表後續緊縮時點仍有不確定性，市場尚未完全定案。

實質殖利率清楚指出存續期間損失的主要來源。10年期實質殖利率上升6個基點至2.47%，幾乎涵蓋名目殖利率全部漲幅；損益兩平通膨率僅上升1個基點。5年期實質殖利率也上升5個基點至2.19%，30年期實質殖利率則上升5個基點至3.03%。對長期公共與民間投資而言，後者仍是異常高的報酬門檻。油價確實推高通膨補償，但更強烈的重新定價，出現在政策與供給不確定時，投資人持有存續期間所要求的實質報酬。

名目與實質殖利率的差異，也限制了政策公信力受損的解讀。殖利率上升、美元卻走弱，顯示市場對聯準會反應函數感到不安；損益兩平通膨率小幅走高，也表示投資人並未忽視通膨風險。然而，10年期損益兩平通膨率為2.28%，全月僅上升4個基點，實質殖利率同期卻上升27個基點。市場正大幅提高實質存續期間與不確定性的定價，但並未計入平均通膨永久且等比例上升。

成交活動顯示，本次收盤價經得起可觀交易量的檢驗。美國公債現券面額成交量達$1.92兆，較前一交易日增加32.4%；名目附息券成交量增加33.4%至$1.52兆。7年至10年期區間增加56.4%至$2,790億，5年至7年期成交量幾乎倍增至$1,730億，TIPS成交量則增加191%至$1,212億。成交量本身包含雙向交易，但集中在這些區間，顯示實質殖利率與指標天期走勢，是經由廣泛價格發現形成，而不是尾盤交易清淡留下的價格。

尾盤指數再平衡確實帶來買盤，30年期殖利率觸及5.28%後，盤中極端走勢也有所收斂，但當日行情並未逆轉。20年以上美國公債指數單日下跌0.69%，7月全月下跌3.87%；相較之下，1年至3年期指數單日下跌0.04%，全月上漲0.17%。因此，現券曲線與指數報酬傳達的是同一項存續期間訊息，不需要另行推導利差。

下檔避險也變得更昂貴。1個月期、25 delta賣權相對買權的溢價，升至約5個月高點；相關選擇權結構押注10年期殖利率接近4.8%至4.9%，30年期接近5.3%至5.42%。MOVE指數仍相對平穩，代表壓力集中在避險需求不對稱，而不是波動率全面飆升。投資人付出的，正是長端賣壓延續的特定風險溢價。

供給是連結政策不確定性與避險偏斜的未解環節。市場預期8月至10月再融資公告將維持標售規模不變，但投資人密切留意，措辭是否開始為2027年擴大附息券發行預作準備。同時，美國財政部正評估，是否把接近$1兆的現金餘額，部分投入規模約$13兆的附買回市場。若準備金下降，這項機制尤其可能緩和交割、繳稅日與報表期附近的融資壓力；不過，交易商承作能力疑慮與估計報酬有限，是否採行仍有不確定性。

利率市場的結論是：實質殖利率領漲，債券熊市行情重新展開；短端重新加入，並未取代既有長端問題。油價、就業成本與聯準會官員異議，提高延後緊縮的代價，再融資不確定性則讓供給溢價延續。曲線變動幅度不大，不應掩蓋市場狀態已經轉變：10年期殖利率4.75%、30年期5.27%，與時點仍不透明的政策路徑並存，使現券存續期間與防範進一步損失的避險成本同樣高昂。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

整體信用市場承受住美國公債賣壓，單日損傷有限，但存續期間仍是總體報酬的主要拖累。LQD下跌0.15%，HYG上漲0.01%，JNK上漲0.02%。長天期AAA至A級與BBB級公司債指數分別下跌0.29%與0.25%，跌幅小於20年以上美國公債指數的0.69%。相較政府債券存續期間，信用債總報酬展現韌性；但兩項長天期公司債指數全月仍分別下跌4.58%與4.19%。

信用市場最重要的新變化，是仍能完成交易的發行人，與融資仰賴樂觀假設或薄弱控管的發行人之間，差距進一步拉大。本週稍早，CoreWeave與Proofpoint只有提高利差並強化貸方保障，才保住融資管道。到了週五，案例進一步下沉至較低信用品質。Cable One規劃中的融資，即使討論殖利率已達12%，交易仍有破局風險；部分既有第一順位留置權貸款的交易殖利率則接近18%。

GTCR行使賣回權後，Cable One必須籌措約$10億，用於強制買下Mega Broadband Investments剩餘55%股權，並展延既有債務。潛在貸方要求設置風險隔離，防止母公司補貼Mega Broadband沉重的債務。Cable One至少背負$30億長期債務，自由現金流有限，又面臨住宅寬頻市場競爭壓力。因此，融資難題不只是指標利率偏高，而是資本結構爭議：收購義務的經濟效益惡化後，新資金能否與這項義務有效隔離。

Extenet則把先前已浮現的流動性警訊，轉化成實際違約與債權人控管問題。約$5億資產擔保證券的利息於7月27日到期，卻未支付。付款管理機構也表示，原應交付債券持有人的收款遭存入其他帳戶，部分留置權也不再具備完善效力。Extenet仍在協商利息暫緩追究協議，但未付款、現金流遭轉移與擔保權完善性受損同時出現，使回收前景比一般展期案件更差。

Extenet事件之所以值得數位基礎設施市場關注，是公司6月警告現金只夠支應數日以前，營收僅小幅下滑。光纖、小型基地台與5G融資過去能吸引資金，是因貸方相信合約型基礎設施現金流與擔保權益足以提供保障。突發現金短缺若又伴隨控管違規指控，市場焦點就會從產業成長轉向帳戶管理、留置權持續有效性與付款順位執行能力。這雖是個別發行人事件，卻也會改變類似結構的承銷方式。

市政債則出現更廣泛的承接問題，主因是利率與供給，而不是信用品質崩潰。截至週四，市政債指數下跌1.72%，7月表現可能創2003年以來最差，儘管夏季的息票支付與贖回通常會支撐需求。全月發行量約$470億，高於一般7月步調，長天期美國公債殖利率又逼近19年高點。兩股壓力交會，使市政債相對美國公債的評價，落入今年最便宜的區間之一。

發行管線仍然活躍。醫院今年以來已發行約$267億，Northwell Healthcare另正考慮透過紐約州宿舍管理局，發行最高$8億免稅債券。交易定價前，這筆潛在供給尚不能證明需求品質；它只能顯示，市場經歷疲弱月份後，仍須承接可觀的醫療照護債券供給。因此，市政債整體壓力較像存續期間與發行日程問題，與Extenet及Cable One的現金控管和槓桿問題不同。

融資市場本身並未在同一交易日出現急性壓力。美國財政部的附買回提案仍處於探索階段，目的是降低未來一般帳戶餘額變動引發的波動，並非因應當前市場失靈。準備金較稀缺時，財政部可依此構想把現金投入附買回市場，可能降低現金餘額回補對短端的衝擊。不過，作業負擔與占用交易商資產負債表的風險，使這項提案目前仍難有定論。週五的失序集中在長存續期間定價與個別借款人結構，而不是擔保美元融資的基本可得性。

貸方議價權的轉變，不只出現在當日幾個受壓案例。美國企業今年已發行近$2,000億非投資等級債券，較2025年同期增加約9%；高評級債券發行量則增加三分之一，達$1.3兆。槓桿貸款平均價格由1月的97美分降至95.3美分，至2028年約有$2,400億到期。CoreWeave與Proofpoint因而不是孤立事件，而是大量供給終結多年借款人友善條件後，貸方得以要求更高收益與更強保障的代表。能源生產商提供重要的現金流反例。油價衝擊推升獲利後，Exxon第2季減少逾$70億淨負債，Chevron投入創紀錄的$84億償債，Shell也降低約$108億淨負債。較高商品現金流正在修復這些資產負債表，但同時也透過通膨與利率壓迫其他借款人。因此，信用市場的整體訊息是：流動性運作正常、融資紀律明顯收緊，而且內部融資能力差距很大。高收益債基金持穩，公司債存續期間單日表現優於相近存續期間的美國公債。同時，市政債大量供給壓倒有利的季節性需求；Cable One已不能假定兩位數殖利率足以完成交易；Extenet違約則引發擔保品控管疑慮。高實質殖利率並未關閉所有市場，卻讓新券讓利、風險隔離、攤還條件、內部去槓桿與可執行的現金管理，成為較弱借款人能否融資的決定性因素。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

海外利率強化美國通膨溢價，但各地政策透過不同管道傳導。歐元區7月通膨由2.8%加速至2.9%，能源價格上漲10%，服務通膨及排除波動較大食品與燃料的指標也雙雙轉強。德國10年期公債殖利率上升1個基點至3.16%；貨幣市場仍估計歐洲央行9月升息25個基點的機率為90%，並計入年底前升息42個基點。美國公債遭到拋售之際，這份數據直接形成海外存續期間逆風。

法國數據顯示，歐元區平均通膨上升並非只是能源基期效應。消費者通膨升至2.4%，高於調查中所有預測；預估中位數為2.0%。服務通膨則由1.9%升至2.3%。加上歐元區第2季產出增速創逾1年最快，且是預期的2倍，這些數據降低歐洲央行再次升息的經濟代價。油價高漲仍是最初衝擊，但服務與薪資是否轉強，將決定壓力會不會持續。

日本央行在6月升息後，以8比1票數將政策利率維持在1%，但總裁植田和男使9月起的每次會議，都成為可能採取緊縮行動的時點。他警告基礎通膨正接近2%目標，意味通膨高於預期的代價增加；若金融情勢持續過度寬鬆，升息步調可能加快。交換市場估計10月前再次升息的機率為89%。植田並未明示9月一定行動，但這次按兵不動仍比例行決策更偏鷹派。

數據足以支持警戒，卻未呈現全面強勁的經濟。東京7月排除生鮮食品後CPI上升1.9%，高於調查預估的1.8%；整體通膨與排除生鮮食品及能源後的指標均為2%。服務價格增速小幅升至1.2%。6月工業生產較5月成長1.3%，零售銷售則月減4.1%、年增僅0.5%。日本央行將本財政年度經濟成長預測上調至0.6%，但受補貼影響，又把通膨預測由2.8%下調至2.5%，因此政策仍對實際物價與匯率走勢敏感。

匯率操作為日本央行爭取時間，卻也另闢一條全球傳導管道。市場估計日本週四干預規模約8.45兆日圓，相當於$528億，日圓兌美元一度上漲3.3%。週五傳出第二次操作，加上紐約聯準銀行詢價與美國財政部協調，帶動日圓上漲約1.3%至157.28。干預可稍微降低輸入性通膨；但如此龐大的規模也凸顯，日本央行1%的政策利率仍遠低於美國利率區間，現貨干預無法永久取代政策趨同。

日圓走強對美國公債有兩股相反作用。一方面，日圓升值可降低日本輸入性物價壓力，也降低日本央行加速緊縮的急迫性，進而抑制日本公債殖利率上升。另一方面，直接干預與未來日本利率走高，也可能減少投資海外長存續期間資產的資源或誘因。美國公債殖利率上升，美元卻因干預管道與市場普遍質疑聯準會公信力而走弱，使美國殖利率缺少通常伴隨的匯率確認。

英國則帶來更長期的能源警訊。英格蘭銀行首席經濟學家Huw Pill表示，伊朗戰爭引發的大宗商品波動可能延續至2027年。基準預測顯示，通膨將在今年底觸及3.2%高點；不利能源情境則會使通膨在2027年升至4.5%，並需要從目前3.75%的水準大幅升息。能源價格已較戰前高出20%。英格蘭銀行前一日才淡化立即升息的可能性，但Pill提出的情境，限制了這項指引能為存續期間帶來的利多。

中國也在擴充投資人持有與避險本地存續期間的市場基礎設施。香港準備重新推出5年期中國公債期貨，合約規模為CNY50萬、採現金結算；2017年與2024年的先前嘗試，都未能建立持久市場。境外投資人持有的中國境內公債，已由2017年中約CNY4,500億增加至CNY2兆。這項產品是否真正重要，仍取決於持續流動性，以及是否實際用於基差、曲線與附買回連結策略；但它降低了把中國公債視為獨立全球利率配置的一項操作障礙。全球因素對美國存續期間的淨影響偏向緊縮。歐元區通膨強化再次升息的理由；日本一面干預匯市，一面保留更具可能性的緊縮路徑；英國即使維持利率不變，能源風險的尾端仍厚。任何單一結果都不能機械式解釋美國公債的全部走勢，但連同其他利率市場改善的准入條件，這些因素提高海外殖利率替代選項，使日本投資人需求更為複雜，也削弱聯準會等待期間，全球央行將同步提供存續期間需求的論點。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

即使美元走弱，新興市場債仍受美國實質利率衝擊壓制。EMB下跌0.14%，15年以上新興市場美元主權債指數下跌0.21%，美元指數也下跌0.21%至99.80。這種分歧與前一交易日相似：匯率條件並未顯示普遍美元短缺，但10年期美國公債殖利率4.75%、長債殖利率5.27%，提高長天期硬通貨現金流的折現負擔。

哥倫比亞帶來最明確的本地政策意外。央行將政策利率維持在12%，與受訪27位經濟學家中23位預期升息不同；4位官員投票維持不變，3位支持升息50個基點。央行理事會也宣布，計畫增持最高$40億外匯存底。披索今年已升值近20%，既降低輸入性通膨，也讓決策者有暫停升息的空間；但央行買進外匯存底，可能削弱同一層匯率緩衝。

維持利率不變，不代表哥倫比亞緊縮循環已經結束。通膨仍高於6%，央行目標為3%、容忍區間正負1個百分點；壓力來自擴張性財政政策、最低工資調升23%，以及食品與能源衝擊。獨立財政委員會預期赤字將超過GDP的7%。央行總裁Leonardo Villar仍保留未來升息的可能性，因此9月會議將檢驗：新政府上任後，匯率強勢能否繼續抵銷財政與薪資壓力。

南非對通膨目標制度展現較高信心，儘管油價衝擊尚未完全逆轉。伊朗戰爭初期，10年期公債殖利率一度觸及9.5%，之後已回落至約8.7%，但仍高於衝突前約8%的水準。5月升息後，央行把政策利率維持在7%，取得耐心觀望的空間。6月通膨為5%，仍高於新的3%目標，因此市場韌性仰賴政策公信力，相信油價衝擊終將消退，而不是通膨已經完成降溫。

Pemex顯示，油價上漲可以改善當期獲利，卻修復不了準主權企業的資產負債表。公司第2季獲利180億披索，相當於$10億；原油與凝析油產量較上年同期增加1.7%，至每日166萬桶。金融債務仍達$775億。政府今年已編列$140億支援其債務，Fitch則估計年底前另有$100億營運資金缺口。

墨西哥財政部長排除今年再向Pemex提供國家資金，即使公司正討論2027年預算支援與可能的再融資。原油價格上漲雖能改善現金創造能力與主權財政收入，卻沒有消除轉嫁給國家的再融資負擔。產量仍只有歷史高峰約一半，國際合作夥伴投入速度也偏慢，因此Pemex依舊是獨立的資產負債表風險，而不是油價上漲的直接受益者。

市場制度又增加一層新興市場分歧。菲律賓準備在預期納入JPMorgan指數前，把20%預扣稅的影響自本地債券定價中移除，使規模$2,300億的市場更接近全球慣例，但未持有至到期的既有投資人可能面臨評價損失。印度的指數時程則朝相反方向發展：即使政府取消外國投資人的預扣稅與資本利得稅，6月5日後也有約$50億流入合格債券，Bloomberg仍因各投資地區的執行尚未完備，延後把印度納入全球綜合債券指數。印度10年期殖利率上升3個基點至6.84%，交易員預期還可能再調整5至10個基點。羅馬尼亞則處於財政與評級邊界。政府申訴並補充資料後，Fitch才確認最低投資等級BBB-，展望維持負向。財政赤字預估由2024年超過GDP的9%，降至今年低於6%，但政治不確定性與2028年選舉週期仍威脅後續整頓。新興市場的結論是：在昂貴的共同折現率與不均等市場准入下，市場分歧持續存在。哥倫比亞利用匯率強勢延後升息，同時增持外匯存底；南非仰賴通膨目標公信力，暫時忽略油價衝擊；Pemex則把較高油價轉化為獲利，卻仍未取得財務獨立。菲律賓調整定價慣例；印度則發現稅制改革不保證立即納入指數；羅馬尼亞保住投資等級，但財政警訊未除。美元走弱，避免美國公債賣壓演變成廣泛流動性事件，卻幾乎沒有降低財政能力、政策公信力、操作准入與硬通貨債務到期結構的重要性。

## 跨資產

股市表現不支持廣泛成長疑慮或融資恐慌。S&P 500上漲0.70%，Nasdaq 100上漲0.60%，VIX下跌6.44%至15.99。半導體指數收盤僅上漲0.07%，全週仍下跌4.30%，全月下跌20.61%。整體風險偏好可以和美國公債高殖利率並存，但資本密集的AI產業仍未出現更強反彈，市場對支出回報與債務承接的疑慮尚未消除。

油價確認眼前的通膨衝擊。WTI上漲1.29%至$84.67，Brent上漲1.22%至$90.12。兩者全週仍下跌，但全月漲幅均超過21%。單日漲幅有助解釋10年期損益兩平通膨率上升1個基點；實質殖利率升幅遠大於此，則證明油價只是放大因素，不是美國公債遭拋售的唯一原因。

美元與黃金走勢，讓單純的通膨避險解讀難以成立。即使美國殖利率上升，美元指數仍跌至99.80，部分原因是協同行動支撐日圓；黃金下跌1.24%至$4,049.10，波動率也回落。美國公債與美元同步走弱，保留了市場對公信力的疑慮；但黃金與VIX下跌，並不支持信心全面流失的判斷。跨資產表現指向實質存續期間與政策不確定性的集中重新定價，信用與股票市場流動性仍正常運作。

## 前瞻市場意涵

8月7日美國就業報告，是下一項明確檢驗，用來判斷週五就業成本上升0.9%，是否屬於持續性勞動通膨管道。調查中位數預期非農就業增加85,000人，6月為增加57,000人，失業率則維持在4.2%。若新增就業明顯高於85,000人，尤其失業率保持穩定，將強化異議官員所稱目前政策限制性不足的論點，使2年期殖利率與長天期實質殖利率持續面臨上行風險。若就業數據較弱，且後續物價也轉弱，實質殖利率與損益兩平通膨率必須同步下降，才能扭轉目前市場狀態；若債市上漲只來自通膨補償下降，實質存續期間負擔仍然存在。

8月至10月再融資公告，可把財政供給與聯準會公信力溢價區分開來。市場預期標售規模維持不變，因此關鍵在於美國財政部是否延續附息券增發時點延後的指引，或開始讓投資人為2027年擴大發行預作準備。若指引穩定，後續標售指標也維持有序，可消除一項近期長端不確定性；若提前釋出供給訊號，則會證實市場確實需要在10年期殖利率4.9%、30年期5.3%至5.42%附近買進避險。將財政部現金投入附買回市場，則透過另一條到期管道傳導：可行的設計能平滑交割相關融資壓力，卻無法解決附息券需求擴大所造成的存續期間承接問題。

海外政策與初級信用市場，將共同決定美國利率衝擊是否維持集中。歐洲央行預計9月決策，8月歐元區通膨必須先顯示，7月能源價格上漲10%是否正傳導至服務；日本央行9月18日會議則須證明，日圓能否在不反覆干預，也不造成日本公債殖利率失序上升的情況下維持穩定。海外通膨下降、日圓持續穩定，可降低海外資產與美國公債存續期間爭奪需求的壓力。信用市場方面，Cable One下一次融資條件、Northwell規劃中的市政債發行，以及後續AI或軟體業交易，將顯示投資人能否透過新券讓利與可執行的保障條款承接風險。若交易順利定價、次級市場表現穩定，問題將維持在個別發行人；若再次延後、以兩位數殖利率成交，或要求更嚴格的風險隔離，則代表高實質利率正把貸方主導的條件重設擴大至更多市場。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

The July 31 Treasury close turned the prior session's consolidation into a renewed, broad selloff. The 2-year yield rose 5 basis points to 4.28%, the 5- and 10-year yields each climbed 7 basis points to 4.45% and 4.75%, and the 30-year added 6 basis points to 5.27%. The move restored pressure across the policy-sensitive front end and the long end after July 30 had left every benchmark tenor only 1 basis point higher. It also carried the 10-year above its post-Fed peak and left the long bond near the highest yield region since 2007.

The dominant change was a harder market judgment on delayed Fed restraint. Statements from the three officials who dissented from the 9-3 decision to hold the funds range at 3.5% to 3.75% linked current inaction to the risk of sharper tightening later. That message had direct price impact: the selloff began in 2- to 5-year maturities, then migrated outward as investors demanded more compensation for persistent inflation. A 0.9% rise in Q2 employment costs, above the median estimate, denied the market the cleaner wage disinflation it needed after June PCE prices fell 0.1%.

Oil and foreign rates reinforced that policy challenge. WTI rose 1.29% to $84.67 and Brent gained 1.22% to $90.12 as renewed supply concerns built into the weekend. Euro-area inflation accelerated to 2.9%, with energy up 10%, pushing German yields higher and strengthening expectations for another ECB increase. The US selloff was therefore not solely a communication premium around Chairman Kevin Warsh. It combined a less predictable reaction function with fresh evidence that wage and energy pressure could keep the inflation burden active across jurisdictions.

The composition still argues against treating the entire move as an inflation-expectations shock. The 10-year real yield rose 6 basis points to 2.47%, accounting for most of the 7-basis-point nominal increase, while the 10-year breakeven edged only 1 basis point higher to 2.28%. Over July, the 10-year real yield rose 27 basis points and the nominal yield 31 basis points. Required real returns, uncertainty over the policy path and the approaching refunding announcement were more important than a wholesale de-anchoring of inflation compensation.

Credit and cross assets kept the rates shock from becoming a generalized liquidation. LQD fell 0.15%, consistent with its duration exposure, while HYG and JNK were nearly unchanged. The S&P 500 gained 0.70%, the VIX fell 6.44% to 15.99 and the dollar slipped 0.21% despite higher US yields. Financing discipline nevertheless tightened at the weaker edges: Cable One struggled to secure about $1 billion for a mandatory acquisition, Extenet missed interest on asset-backed bonds, and municipal debt suffered an unusually poor July under heavy supply. The regime remained liquid, but high real yields were exposing structure, refinancing dependence and issuer-specific control failures.

The close consequently deepened the same regime established after the Fed meeting rather than creating a new growth scare. Immediate policy relief had already been removed; Friday added evidence that the front end could reprice upward even as the long end retained a fiscal and credibility premium. Hawkish BOJ guidance and forceful yen intervention offered a partial counterweight by reducing imported inflation pressure in Japan, yet they also raised the return available on Japanese assets and the possibility of reserve-related spillover. The central fixed-income question is now whether incoming US data and stable Treasury coupon guidance can lower real yields before selective credit strain becomes a broader absorption problem.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

Friday's move was broad, with a modest belly bias rather than another dramatic steepener. The 5- and 10-year sectors rose 7 basis points, compared with 5 basis points in the 2-year and 6 basis points in the 30-year. The 2s10s curve widened 2 basis points to 47, while 2s30s steepened 1 basis point to 99. That differs from the July 29 reaction, when the Fed hold drove the 2-year lower and the 30-year sharply higher. The current session removed much of the front-end relief while preserving nearly all of the post-meeting long-end premium.

The curve's monthly horizon is more restrictive than its small daily steepening. The 2-year ended July 14 basis points higher, the 5-year 26 basis points higher, the 10-year 31 basis points higher and the 30-year 36 basis points higher. This increasingly large rise toward longer maturities reflects more than expectations for a single rate increase. It incorporates the risk that persistent inflation, large future financing needs and limited policy guidance keep the equilibrium discount rate elevated even if the next FOMC decision is delayed.

The three dissenters made the near-term policy channel explicit. Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack argued that policy was not sufficiently restrictive, Minneapolis Fed President Neel Kashkari supported incremental tightening while data arrive, and Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said modest action now could reduce the need for sharper action later. Logan also judged inflation to be moving toward the mid-2% range rather than 2%, even after allowing for supply shocks and productivity. Their shared concern was not merely July energy volatility; it was that labor demand, spending and financial conditions remained too firm for inflation to finish the return to target unaided.

Employment costs supplied a same-session check on that argument. The Q2 gauge rose 0.9%, exceeding the median estimate. The miss was not large enough by itself to establish renewed wage acceleration, but its direction mattered in a market seeking lower inflation readings to validate the Fed's patience. Combined with the oil rise, it helped the initial front-end selloff spread toward maturities carrying longer inflation and term-premium exposure. The 2-year close at 4.28% still sat below the 4.37% funds-range midpoint, leaving the timing of additional restraint uncertain rather than fully resolved.

Real yields locate the principal source of the duration loss. The 10-year real yield's 6-basis-point increase to 2.47% matched almost the entire nominal move, whereas the breakeven rose only 1 basis point. The 5-year real yield also gained 5 basis points to 2.19%, and the 30-year real yield increased 5 basis points to 3.03%. The latter remained an unusually high hurdle for long-lived public and private investment. Inflation compensation reacted to oil, but the more forceful repricing was in the real return required to own duration under uncertain policy and supply.

That distinction qualifies the policy-credibility reading. A weaker dollar alongside higher yields indicates unease about the Fed's reaction function, and the modest rise in breakevens shows that the market did not dismiss inflation risk. Yet the 2.28% 10-year breakeven was only 4 basis points higher over the month, compared with a 27-basis-point rise in the real yield. The market was charging heavily for real duration and uncertainty without pricing a proportionate permanent rise in average inflation.

Trading activity confirms that the close survived substantial turnover. Treasury cash par volume reached $1.92 trillion, up 32.4% from the prior session, and nominal-coupon activity rose 33.4% to $1.52 trillion. The 7- to 10-year bucket increased 56.4% to $279 billion, while 5- to 7-year activity almost doubled to $173 billion. TIPS volume rose 191% to $121.2 billion. These are two-way measures, but the concentration shows that the real-yield and benchmark-tenor moves were established through broad price discovery rather than a thin late-session mark.

Late index rebalancing did generate demand and pared the intraday extremes after the 30-year yield reached 5.28%. It did not reverse the session. The 20-year-plus Treasury index lost 0.69% on the day and 3.87% over July, compared with a 0.04% daily decline and a 0.17% monthly gain in the 1- to 3-year index. The cash curve and index returns therefore tell the same duration story without requiring a separate spread inference.

Downside hedging also became more expensive. The premium for 1-month, 25-delta puts over calls reached its highest level in about 5 months, with option structures targeting 10-year yields near 4.8% to 4.9% and 30-year yields around 5.3% to 5.42%. The MOVE Index remained comparatively subdued, so the stress was concentrated in the asymmetry of protection rather than a generalized volatility surge. Investors were paying specifically for the risk that the long-end selloff extends.

Supply is the unresolved bridge between policy uncertainty and that skew. The August-to-October refunding announcement was expected to leave auction sizes steady, but investors were alert to language preparing larger coupon issuance in 2027. At the same time, Treasury was exploring whether part of a cash balance near $1 trillion could be invested in the roughly $13 trillion repo market. Such a program could smooth funding pressure around settlements, tax dates and reporting periods, particularly if reserves decline, although dealer-capacity concerns and a modest estimated return make adoption uncertain.

The rates conclusion is a renewed bear move led by real yields, with the front end rejoining rather than displacing the long-end problem. Oil, employment costs and Fed dissents made delayed tightening more costly; refunding uncertainty kept the supply premium alive. Small curve changes should not obscure the regime shift: a 4.75% 10-year and 5.27% 30-year now coexist with a policy path whose timing remains opaque, leaving both cash duration and protection against further losses expensive.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Broad credit absorbed the Treasury selloff with limited same-day damage, but duration remained the main aggregate drag. LQD fell 0.15%, while HYG rose 0.01% and JNK gained 0.02%. Long-maturity AAA-to-A and BBB corporate indices declined 0.29% and 0.25%, less than the 0.69% loss in the 20-year-plus Treasury index. These returns show resilience in credit total returns relative to government duration; they do not erase the 4.58% and 4.19% monthly losses in the two long corporate indices.

The important credit delta was a sharper divide between issuers that could still transact and those whose financing depended on aggressive assumptions or weak controls. Earlier in the week, CoreWeave and Proofpoint had preserved access only after paying higher margins and strengthening lender protections. Friday's cases moved farther down the quality spectrum. Cable One's contemplated financing was at risk even with discussions around a 12% yield, while parts of its existing first-lien loan traded at yields near 18%.

Cable One needed roughly $1 billion to fund the mandatory purchase of the remaining 55% of Mega Broadband Investments after GTCR exercised a put option and to extend existing debt. Prospective lenders sought ring-fencing that would prevent the parent from subsidizing Mega Broadband's heavy obligations. With at least $3 billion of long-term debt, limited free cash flow and competitive pressure in residential broadband, the financing challenge was not simply a high benchmark rate. It was a capital-structure dispute over whether new money could be insulated from an acquisition obligation whose economics had deteriorated.

Extenet converted a previously visible liquidity warning into a realized default and a creditor-control problem. Interest on about $500 million of asset-backed securities was due July 27 and went unpaid. The payment administrator also said collections intended for bondholders had been deposited elsewhere and that some liens had ceased to be perfected. Extenet was still negotiating an interest-forbearance agreement, but the combination of missed payment, diverted cash flows and impaired collateral perfection weakened recoverability beyond an ordinary extension request.

The Extenet episode matters for digital infrastructure because revenues had declined only slightly before the company warned in June that it was days from running out of cash. Fiber, small-cell and 5G financing had attracted capital on the premise that contracted infrastructure cash flows and security interests would protect lenders. A sudden cash shortfall accompanied by alleged control violations shifts the focus from sector growth to account administration, lien durability and the ability to enforce payment waterfalls. It is an issuer-specific failure with implications for how similar structures are underwritten.

Municipals showed a broader absorption problem driven by rates and supply rather than a collapse in credit quality. The municipal index was down 1.72% through Thursday, on course for its worst July since 2003, even though summer coupon payments and redemptions normally support demand. Issuance reached roughly $47 billion during the month, above the usual July pace, just as long Treasury yields approached 19-year highs. The collision left municipal valuations at some of their cheapest levels of the year relative to Treasuries.

The pipeline remained active. Northwell Healthcare was considering as much as $800 million of tax-exempt bonds through New York's Dormitory Authority after hospitals had already issued about $26.7 billion year to date. That prospective sale does not establish demand quality before pricing, but it shows that the market still had to absorb sizeable health-care supply after the weak month. Municipal pressure therefore looked like a duration-and-calendar problem at the broad level, distinct from the cash-control and leverage problems at Extenet and Cable One.

Funding markets themselves did not display acute same-session stress. The Treasury's repo proposal was exploratory and aimed at reducing future volatility from changes in its general account, not a response to a current seizure. The idea could place Treasury cash into repo when reserves are scarcer, potentially reducing the front-end footprint of cash-balance rebuilding. Its operational burden and the risk of consuming dealer balance sheet limit the conclusion. Friday's disorder was in long-duration pricing and selected borrower structures, not in the basic availability of secured dollar funding.

The shift in bargaining power extended beyond the day's distressed cases. US companies had sold almost $200 billion of junk bonds during the year, about 9% more than at the same point in 2025, while high-grade issuance had increased by one-third to $1.3 trillion. Average leveraged-loan prices had fallen to 95.3 cents from 97 cents in January, with about $240 billion due through 2028. CoreWeave and Proofpoint were therefore examples of a broader supply regime in which lenders could demand yield and protection after years of borrower-friendly terms. Energy producers supplied an important cash-flow counterexample. Exxon reduced net debt by more than $7 billion during Q2, Chevron directed a record $8.4 billion to debt reduction, and Shell cut net debt by about $10.8 billion as the oil shock lifted profits. Higher commodity cash flow was repairing these balance sheets even while it raised inflation and rate pressure for other borrowers. The aggregate credit message is therefore functional liquidity under materially tighter discipline and sharply different internal funding capacity. High-yield funds held steady and corporate duration outperformed comparable Treasury duration on the day. At the same time, heavy municipal supply defeated favorable seasonal demand, Cable One could not assume that a double-digit yield would complete its transaction, and Extenet's default raised questions about collateral control. Higher real yields are not closing every market; they are making concession, ring-fencing, amortization, internal deleveraging and enforceable cash management decisive for weaker borrowers.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

Foreign rates reinforced the US inflation premium, though the policy channels differed. Euro-area inflation accelerated to 2.9% in July from 2.8%, with energy prices up 10% and both services and the measure excluding volatile food and fuel strengthening. German 10-year yields rose 1 basis point to 3.16%, and money markets continued to assign a 90% likelihood to a 25-basis-point ECB increase in September while pricing 42 basis points by year-end. The result supplied a direct foreign-duration headwind as Treasuries sold off.

France showed why the regional average was not merely an energy-base effect. Consumer inflation rose to 2.4%, above every forecast in the survey, whose median expected 2.0%. Services inflation increased to 2.3% from 1.9%. Combined with Q2 euro-area output growing at the strongest pace in more than a year and twice the expected rate, the release reduced the economic cost of another ECB increase. Elevated oil remains the initiating shock, but firmer services and wages determine whether it becomes persistent.

The BOJ held its policy rate at 1% by an 8-1 vote after June's increase, yet Governor Kazuo Ueda made every meeting from September a credible tightening venue. He warned that underlying inflation was approaching the 2% objective, making upside surprises more costly, and said the pace of increases could accelerate if financial conditions remained too accommodative. Swaps placed an 89% probability on another increase by October. This was more hawkish than a routine hold, even though Ueda stopped short of forcing a September move.

The data justified vigilance without presenting a uniformly strong economy. Tokyo CPI excluding fresh food rose 1.9% in July, above the 1.8% survey estimate, while both overall inflation and the measure excluding fresh food and energy were 2%. Service-price growth edged up to 1.2%. June industrial production gained 1.3% from May, but retail sales fell 4.1% on the month and rose only 0.5% from a year earlier. The BOJ upgraded fiscal-year growth to 0.6% while lowering its inflation forecast to 2.5% from 2.8% because of subsidies, leaving policy sensitive to realized prices and the currency.

Currency action bought the BOJ time but created a separate global transmission channel. Japan's Thursday intervention was estimated at about JPY8.45 trillion, or $52.8 billion, and lifted the yen as much as 3.3% against the dollar. On Friday, reports of a second operation, New York Fed rate checks and US Treasury coordination helped the yen gain about 1.3% to 157.28. The action reduces imported inflation at the margin; its scale also underscores that a 1% BOJ rate remains far below the US range and that spot intervention cannot permanently substitute for policy convergence.

For Treasuries, a firmer yen has competing effects. It can reduce Japan's imported-price pressure and the urgency of accelerated BOJ tightening, which would contain the rise in JGB yields. Direct intervention and higher prospective domestic rates can also reduce the resources or incentive available for foreign-duration purchases. The dollar's decline despite rising Treasury yields reflected this intervention channel and broader concern about the Fed's credibility, leaving US yields without their usual currency confirmation.

Britain added a longer-horizon energy warning. BOE Chief Economist Huw Pill said commodity volatility from the Iran war could persist into 2027. The central forecast placed inflation at a 3.2% peak late in the year, while an adverse energy scenario lifted it to 4.5% in 2027 and required materially higher rates from the current 3.75%. Energy prices were already 20% above prewar levels. The BOE had pushed back against an imminent hike the previous day, but Pill's scenarios limited the duration relief available from that guidance.

China was also expanding the infrastructure for investors to hold and hedge local duration. Hong Kong was preparing to relaunch 5-year Chinese government-bond futures with a CNY500,000 cash-settled contract, after earlier attempts in 2017 and 2024 failed to establish a durable market. Foreign holdings of onshore Chinese government debt had risen to CNY2 trillion from about CNY450 billion in mid-2017. The product's significance would depend on sustained liquidity and actual use in basis, curve and repo-linked strategies, but it lowered one operational barrier to treating Chinese bonds as a distinct global rates allocation. The net global impulse was restrictive for US duration. Euro inflation strengthened the case for another hike, Japan paired intervention with a more live tightening path, and the UK retained a fat energy tail even after holding rates. None of these outcomes mechanically caused the full Treasury move. Together with improving access to alternative rates markets, they raised foreign yield options, complicated the Japanese buyer base and weakened the case that global central banks would provide synchronized duration demand while the Fed waited.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Emerging-market debt remained constrained by the US real-rate shock even as the dollar weakened. EMB fell 0.14%, and the 15-year-plus EM dollar sovereign index lost 0.21%, while the Dollar Index declined 0.21% to 99.80. The divergence resembles the prior close: currency conditions were not signaling a generalized dollar shortage, but a 4.75% 10-year Treasury and 5.27% long bond imposed a larger discount on long hard-currency cash flows.

Colombia provided the clearest local-policy surprise. The central bank held its policy rate at 12%, against expectations from 23 of 27 surveyed economists for an increase, with four officials voting to hold and three favoring a 50-basis-point hike. The board also announced an initiative to accumulate as much as $4 billion in reserves. A peso that had gained nearly 20% during the year reduced imported inflation and gave policymakers room to pause, but reserve purchases can weaken that same cushion.

The hold did not end Colombia's tightening cycle. Inflation remained above 6% against a 3% target with a 1-percentage-point tolerance band, reflecting expansionary fiscal policy, a 23% minimum-wage increase and food and energy shocks. The independent fiscal committee expected the deficit to exceed 7% of GDP. Governor Leonardo Villar kept future hikes on the table, making the September meeting a test of whether currency strength can continue offsetting fiscal and wage pressure under a new administration.

South Africa demonstrated greater confidence in an inflation-target regime, although the oil shock was not fully reversed. Its 10-year government yield had recovered to about 8.7% after reaching 9.5% early in the Iran war, but remained above the roughly 8% level before hostilities. The central bank held its policy rate at 7% after a May increase created room for patience. June inflation at 5% still exceeded the new 3% target, so resilience rested on credibility that the shock would fade rather than on already completed disinflation.

Pemex showed how stronger oil can improve current earnings without repairing a quasi-sovereign balance sheet. The company reported an 18 billion peso, or $1 billion, Q2 profit and lifted crude and condensate production 1.7% from a year earlier to 1.66 million barrels a day. Financial debt still stood at $77.5 billion. The government had budgeted $14 billion for debt support this year, while Fitch estimated an additional $10 billion operating shortfall by year-end.

Mexico's finance minister ruled out more state funds for Pemex this year, even as the company discussed support in the 2027 budget and a possible refinancing. Higher crude prices therefore improve cash generation and the sovereign's revenue backdrop, but they do not remove the refinancing transfer to the state. With production still roughly half its historical peak and international partners slow to commit, Pemex remains a distinct balance-sheet risk rather than a straightforward beneficiary of the oil rally.

Market plumbing created another layer of EM dispersion. The Philippines planned to remove the effect of a 20% withholding tax from local-bond pricing ahead of expected JPMorgan index inclusion, bringing its $230 billion market closer to global convention but potentially imposing mark-to-market losses on existing holders who sold before maturity. India moved in the opposite direction on index timing: despite removing withholding and capital-gains taxes and attracting about $5 billion into eligible bonds after June 5, Bloomberg deferred entry into its global aggregate index because implementation was incomplete across investor regions. The 10-year Indian yield rose 3 basis points to 6.84%, and traders anticipated a further 5-to-10-basis-point adjustment. Romania supplied the fiscal-rating boundary. Fitch affirmed BBB-, the lowest investment grade, with a negative outlook only after an appeal and additional government information; the deficit was expected below 6% of GDP from more than 9% in 2024, but political uncertainty and the 2028 election cycle threatened further consolidation. The EM conclusion is persistent dispersion under an expensive common discount rate and uneven market access. Colombia used currency strength to delay a hike while adding reserves, South Africa relied on target credibility to look through oil, and Pemex converted higher prices into profit without achieving financial independence. The Philippines changed pricing conventions, India learned that tax reform did not guarantee immediate index entry, and Romania preserved investment grade without removing its fiscal warning. A softer dollar prevented the Treasury selloff from becoming a broad liquidity event. It did little to reduce the importance of fiscal capacity, policy credibility, operational access and the maturity of hard-currency obligations.

## Cross asset

Equities rejected a broad growth or funding panic. The S&P 500 rose 0.70% and the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.60%, while the VIX fell 6.44% to 15.99. The semiconductor index ended only 0.07% higher and remained down 4.30% over the week and 20.61% over the month. Broad risk appetite could coexist with high Treasury yields, but the capital-intensive AI complex still lacked the stronger rebound that would resolve concerns about spending returns and debt absorption.

Oil confirmed the immediate inflation impulse, with WTI at $84.67 and Brent at $90.12 after gains of 1.29% and 1.22%. Both remained lower over the week but more than 21% higher over the month. The daily rise helped explain the 1-basis-point increase in 10-year breakevens; the much larger real-yield move shows that oil was an amplifier rather than the sole cause of the Treasury selloff.

The dollar and gold qualified a simple inflation-haven interpretation. The Dollar Index fell to 99.80 despite the increase in US yields, partly as coordinated action supported the yen, while gold declined 1.24% to $4,049.10 and volatility eased. Simultaneous Treasury and dollar weakness preserved the credibility concern, but lower gold and VIX readings argued against a wholesale loss of confidence. Cross assets support a concentrated repricing of real duration and policy uncertainty, with credit and equity liquidity still functioning.

## Forward Market Significance

The August 7 US employment report is the next clean test of whether Friday's 0.9% employment-cost increase belongs to a persistent labor-inflation channel. The survey median anticipates an 85,000 payroll gain after 57,000 in June and an unemployment rate holding at 4.2%. Hiring materially above that pace, particularly if unemployment remains steady, would strengthen the dissenters' argument that current policy is not restrictive enough and keep both the 2-year yield and long real yields exposed. A weaker payroll result accompanied by softer subsequent prices would need to lower real yields as well as breakevens to reverse the current regime; a rally delivered only by lower inflation compensation would leave the real-duration burden intact.

The August-to-October refunding announcement separates fiscal supply from the Fed-credibility premium. Auction sizes are expected to remain steady, so the consequential signal is whether Treasury preserves guidance that delays coupon increases or prepares investors for larger 2027 issuance. Stable guidance followed by orderly auction metrics would remove an immediate source of long-end uncertainty, whereas an earlier supply signal would validate the demand for protection around 4.9% in the 10-year and 5.3% to 5.42% in the 30-year. Progress on investing Treasury cash in repo matters through a different maturity channel: a workable design could smooth settlement-related funding pressure, but it would not solve the duration absorption problem created by larger coupon needs.

Foreign policy and primary credit together determine whether the US shock remains concentrated. August euro-area inflation must show whether July's 10% energy rise is passing into services before the expected September ECB decision, while the BOJ's September 18 meeting must show that yen stability can survive without repeated intervention or a disorderly increase in JGB yields. Lower foreign inflation and a durable yen would reduce competition for Treasury duration. In credit, the next Cable One financing terms, Northwell's contemplated municipal sale and subsequent AI or software transactions reveal whether investors can absorb risk through concession and enforceable protections. Successful pricing with stable secondary performance would keep the problem issuer-specific; another delay, double-digit clearing yield or demand for stronger ring-fencing would show high real rates broadening the lender-led reset.

section_summaries.summary: Foreign policy signals reinforced the duration headwind: firmer euro-area inflation supported another ECB increase, the BOJ paired intervention with a live tightening path, and the UK retained a long energy tail. These forces raised foreign yield alternatives and complicated prospective demand for Treasuries.

section_summaries.market_read: Dollar liquidity stayed functional, yet the common real-rate discount kept sovereign dispersion wide.
section_summaries.next_check: Colombia's September decision will test whether currency strength can offset fiscal and wage pressure.
section_summaries.section_title: EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk
section_summaries.summary: EM debt remained exposed to expensive US real rates despite a softer dollar. Colombia used currency strength to pause, South Africa relied on inflation-target credibility, and Pemex's stronger earnings left its refinancing burden intact, preserving dispersion around policy, fiscal capacity and hard-currency maturities.

section_summaries.market_read: Risk appetite remained intact, so the rates shock did not become a general liquidation.
section_summaries.next_check: Track whether equity resilience survives if real yields extend higher and oil stays firm.
section_summaries.summary: Equities and lower volatility rejected a broad growth or funding panic, even as oil amplified the inflation impulse. A weaker dollar and lower gold complicated a simple haven story, leaving cross assets consistent with concentrated real-duration and policy-uncertainty repricing.

section_summaries.market_read: The regime can ease only if real yields fall and absorption remains orderly across channels.
section_summaries.next_check: A lower real-yield response across the coming tests is required to reverse the regime.
section_summaries.summary: Three tests determine whether the shock persists: US employment must validate or weaken the labor-inflation channel, refunding guidance must clarify coupon-supply risk, and foreign policy plus primary credit must show whether duration competition and lender discipline broaden beyond rates.
